The new school building has large classroom spaces with plenty of space for all of the pupils equipment. Every area is fully equipped with ceiling track hoists and there are fully accessible hygiene areas for each pair of classrooms.
There are four specially designed sensory rooms which support pupils who have visual, hearing and other sensory impairments.
To support pupils’ physical development, there is a hydrotherapy pool with hoist access that also has a height adjustable floor and an accessible floor level trampoline in the main hall to allow access to rebound therapy.
Although the outside space will be quite small there are shaded canopy areas outside each class, sensory planting and accessible play equipment

Governance and Partnership Learning
Governors
What do we do?
Governors work with the Leadership Group at the school to promote continuous improvement in the education provided for all the children attending our school. We work together to make decisions on the overall direction of the school and set policies, targets, and development plans. We also decide how to make the best use of the school budget for the benefit of the children’s education. As governors we work as a team, deciding on things jointly and sharing responsibilities for the decisions we make.
Who are the governors?
Our membership is made up of parents, staff, and members of the local community.
Declaration of Interest
Chief Executive Officer for Compass Learning Partnership in Brent.
Member of staff at Trinity School which is within the same LA.
Clerk to the Governors
At Oxlow Bridge School, the full Governing Body meets once every half term. If you wish to contact a Governor please email them c/o office@oxlowbridge.com or If you wish to write to any governor, send it marked ‘Private and Confidential’ to the school and the letter will be passed on unopened. Finally, if you wish to speak to a Governor on the phone, please contact the School Office and arrangements will be made for you to be contacted.
The governing body is responsible for the conduct of its school, and must promote high standards of educational achievement at the school. It is the school’s accountable body and as such:
Partnership Learning

Curriculum and Assessment
Curriculum and Assessment
None of the pupils at Oxlow Bridge are expected to reach the standards to be entered for formal age related testing, although teacher assessment data is submitted to the DFE using the Engagement model.
Oxlow Bridge uses Earwig to record and assess pupils progress against their personalised learning goals.
Within each Key Stage group, our students follow a 4 year topic cycle. Please see further details below.
The plans for Key stage 2 and beyond, are currently in draft format. These will be finalised as the school grows and our students grow into these age groups.

Pupil Premium / Free School Meals
Pupil Premium / Free School Meals
Families can apply for Free School Meals/Pupil Premium, by clicking on the link below
Pupil Premium registration (Free School Meals) - London borough of Barking and Dagenham. All rights reserved.
What is Pupil Premium?
Introduced in 2011, the Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) is a sum of money given to schools each year by the Government to close the attainment gap between disadvantaged pupils and their peers, and to support pupils with parents in the armed forces.
This is based on research showing that children from low income families perform less well at school than their peers. Often, children who are entitled to pupil premium face challenges such as poor language and communication skills, lack of confidence and issues with attendance and punctuality. The pupil premium is intended to directly benefit the children who are eligible, helping to narrow the gap between them and their peers.
The Government has used pupils entitled to Free School meals as an indicator for deprivation, and have deployed a fixed amount of money to schools per pupil, based on the number of pupils registered for ‘Free School meals’ (or ‘Pupil Premium’) over a rolling six-year period. Looked after children and those of service personnel also attract funding.
If you are on a low income or receive Child Benefit and any of these benefits, you could claim free school meals/Pupil Premium for your child:
Income Support
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
The guaranteed element of Pension Credit
You may qualify for free school meals for your child if:
If you are unsure or would like some support with this, please feel free to contact us at office@oxlowbridge.com.
You are an asylum seeker
